news.headline: Karnataka considering law for action against pvt hospitals withholding bodies
news.story_lead: Karnataka considering law for action against pvt hospitals withholding bodies The proposed legislation aims to prevent hospitals from making payment a condition for handing over bodies Karnataka is considering a new law to enable legal action against private hospitals that withhold the bodies of dead patients over unpaid medical bills, state health minister U T Khader said on Monday. The proposed legislation aims to prevent hospitals from making payment a condition for handing over bodies. Khader said the health department plans to consult hospital associations before finalising the proposed changes.
news.full_article_text: Karnataka considering law for action against pvt hospitals withholding bodies The proposed legislation aims to prevent hospitals from making payment a condition for handing over bodies Karnataka is considering a new law to enable legal action against private hospitals that withhold the bodies of dead patients over unpaid medical bills, state health minister U T Khader said on Monday. The proposed legislation aims to prevent hospitals from making payment a condition for handing over bodies. Khader said the health department plans to consult hospital associations before finalising the proposed changes. “If someone dies in a private hospital, the family has to pay money to get the body. This places a financial burden on families already struggling and may not have the money. Hospitals should not withhold bodies to recover dues and make families suffer,” Khader said. He said the government identified shortcomings in the rules introduced in 2007 and 2018 and wants to change the existing framework. “They have not been implemented properly. I want to ensure they are implemented fully. If a private hospital refuses to hand over a body, what should the patient’s relatives do, and what action should follow? We need a new law to address this,” he said. The Karnataka Private Medical Establishments Act, 2007, amended in 2018, requires private medical establishments to hand over a patient’s body immediately without insisting on prior payment of outstanding dues. Hospitals can pursue recovery of unpaid amounts through legal means. Khader said the existing arrangement placed families under pressure to settle bills because they wanted to avoid court proceedings. He said the government was considering changes to prevent families from having to borrow money to secure the release of a relative’s body. Shobha Prakash, president of a private hospitals’ association, said hospitals could face difficulties if they were required to hand over bodies without receiving payment for treatment and medicines provided in intensive care units. “We provide ICU treatment and medicines. It is difficult when we are asked to hand over the body without payment after the patient dies. The minister’s decision is right, but an alternative arrangement is needed. Private hospitals should be consulted on this,” Prakash said. Khader said consultations with hospital associations and other stakeholders would form part of the process of framing the new legislation. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Arun Dev Arun Dev is an Assistant Editor with the Karnataka bureau of Hindustan Times. A journalist for over 10 years, he has written extensively on crime and politics.
bullet_points: Karnataka considering law for action against pvt hospitals withholding bodies
The proposed legislation aims to prevent hospitals from making payment a condition for handing over bodies

Karnataka is considering a new law to enable legal action against private hospitals that withhold the bodies of dead patients over unpaid medical bills, state health minister U T Khader said on Monday. The proposed legislation aims to prevent hospitals from making payment a condition for handing over bodies.

Khader said the health department plans to consult hospital associations before finalising the proposed changes. “If someone dies in a private hospital, the family has to pay money to get the body. This places a financial burden on families already struggling and may not have the money. Hospitals should not withhold bodies to recover dues and make families suffer,” Khader said.

He said the government identified shortcomings in the rules introduced in 2007 and 2018 and wants to change the existing framework. “They have not been implemented properly. I want to ensure they are implemented fully. If a private hospital refuses to hand over a body, what should the patient’s relatives do, and what action should follow? We need a new law to address this,” he said.

The Karnataka Private Medical Establishments Act, 2007, amended in 2018, requires private medical establishments to hand over a patient’s body immediately without insisting on prior payment of outstanding dues. Hospitals can pursue recovery of unpaid amounts through legal means.

Khader said the existing arrangement placed families under pressure to settle bills because they wanted to avoid court proceedings. He said the government was considering changes to prevent families from having to borrow money to secure the release of a relative’s body.

Shobha Prakash, president of a private hospitals’ association, said hospitals could face difficulties if they were required to hand over bodies without receiving payment for treatment and medicines provided in intensive care units. “We provide ICU treatment and medicines. It is difficult when we are asked to hand over the body without payment after the patient dies. The minister’s decision is right, but an alternative arrangement is needed. Private hospitals should be consulted on this,” Prakash

news.headline: September 2026 second warmest on record, global temperatures exceed: C3S
news.story_lead: September 2026 second warmest on record, global temperatures exceed: C3S C3S data had earlier shown August was the joint warmest month ever recorded globally, tied with July 2023 September 2026 was the second warmest September ever recorded globally and marked the second consecutive month in 2026, with global temperatures exceeding 1.5°C above the pre-industrial levels, new data shows. Global temperatures reached 1.63°C above the pre-industrial level in September, continuing a new run of months above 1.5°C which started in August and is expected to continue into 2027, the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) said on Monday. C3S data had earlier shown August was the joint warmest month ever recorded globally, tied with July 2023.
news.full_article_text: September 2026 second warmest on record, global temperatures exceed: C3S C3S data had earlier shown August was the joint warmest month ever recorded globally, tied with July 2023 September 2026 was the second warmest September ever recorded globally and marked the second consecutive month in 2026, with global temperatures exceeding 1.5°C above the pre-industrial levels, new data shows. Global temperatures reached 1.63°C above the pre-industrial level in September, continuing a new run of months above 1.5°C which started in August and is expected to continue into 2027, the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) said on Monday. C3S data had earlier shown August was the joint warmest month ever recorded globally, tied with July 2023. The global average surface air temperature was 1.65°C higher than the estimated pre-industrial baseline this August, also making it the first month to exceed 1.5°C since November 2025, it said. Meanwhile the September average sea surface temperature (SST) is the highest on record for the month, amid strengthening El Niño conditions, C3S said, adding El Niño should continue to strengthen in the equatorial Pacific, likely resulting in one of the strongest El Niño events ever recorded. “The average SST for extra-polar oceans (60°S–60°N) in September 2026 was the highest on record for the month, at 21.05°C, surpassing the previous September record of 20.92°C set in 2023. Meanwhile, around Antarctica, the sea ice extent reached its third-lowest annual winter maximum,” the report said. Copernicus is the Earth observation component of the European Union’s Space programme. It includes assistance from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) -- both as a research institute and operational service which gives global numerical weather predictions. This comes days after the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) on October 8 said El Niño will continue to intensify in the coming months and is likely to see peak levels in December. It is likely to bring above-average temperatures to much of the globe and shift rainfall patterns, increasing the risk of drought and floods in different regions, it had said. Carlo Buontempo, Director of the Copernicus Climate Change Service said September saw exceptionally high temperatures again across parts of Europe after an extreme summer. “We are in a new run of months above 1.5°C, and with a strong El Niño still intensifying it is likely to last into 2027. Crossing the Paris Agreement’s long-term limit is only a matter of time. How far we overshoot, and for how long, is still up to us. Copernicus data to guide that choice are free and open to all,” he said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Jasjeev Gandhiok Jasjeev Gandhiok is an Assistant Editor with Hindustan Times, where he covers environment, climate change, the clean energy transition and wildlife at the National Bureau. Gandhiok has over a decade of experience in journalism and is based in Delhi. He has reported extensively on Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR). This includes the region's air pollution woes, a polluted Yamuna and on urban wildlife still thriving in the region. He joined HT in October 2021. Prior to that, he had five-year stint at The Times of India in Delhi, where he also covered Delhi, with a focus on environment and wildlife. Gandhiok has covered some recent events around the Capital too, ranging from the farmers' protests, the northeast Delhi riots and the CAA-NRC protests, reporting from the ground on all of these. He also travels across the country to report on how environment and climate change impact everyday life, while also writing on endangered species. His reports in 2019 on toxic leachate from Delhi's landfills led to the National Green Tribunal (NGT) taking suo motu cognisance and ultimately asking the state government to start bio-mining to flatten and remove all three landfills in the capital. He also closely tracks the implementation of government policies on climate, renewable energy and environmental protection. His focus remains on impactful, public-interest journalism which explains how environmental decisions affect people's everyday lives. Read More

September 2026 was the second warmest September ever recorded globally and marked the second consecutive month in 2026, with global temperatures exceeding 1.5°C above the pre-industrial levels, new data shows.

Global temperatures reached 1.63°C above the pre-industrial level in September, continuing a new run of months above 1.5°C which started in August and is expected to continue into 2027, the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) said on Monday.

C3S data had earlier shown August was the joint warmest month ever recorded globally, tied with July 2023. The global average surface air temperature was 1.65°C higher than the estimated pre-industrial baseline this August, also making it the first month to exceed 1.5°C since November 2025, it said.

Meanwhile the September average sea surface temperature (SST) is the highest on record for the month, amid strengthening El Niño conditions, C3S said, adding El Niño should continue to strengthen in the equatorial Pacific, likely resulting in one of the strongest El Niño events ever recorded.

“The average SST for extra-polar oceans (60°S–60°N) in September 2026 was the highest on record for the month, at 21.05°C, surpassing the previous September record of 20.92°C set in 2023. Meanwhile, around Antarctica, the sea ice extent reached its third-lowest annual winter maximum,” the report said.

Copernicus is the Earth observation component of the European Union’s Space programme. It includes assistance from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) -- both as a research institute and operational service which gives global numerical weather predictions.

Global temperatures reached 1.63°C above the pre-industrial level in September, continuing a new run of months above 1.5°C which started in August and is expected to continue into 2027, the Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) said on Monday.

C3S data had earlier shown August was the joint warmest month ever recorded globally, tied with July 2023. The global average surface air temperature was 1.65°C higher than the estimated pre-industrial baseline this August, also making it the first month to exceed 1.5°C since November 2025, it said.

Meanwhile the September average sea surface temperature (SST) is the highest on record for the month, amid strengthening El Niño conditions, C3S said, adding El Niño should continue to strengthen in the equatorial Pacific, likely resulting in one of the strongest El Niño events ever recorded.

“The average SST for extra-polar oceans (60°S–60°N) in September 2026 was the highest on record for the month, at 21.05°C, surpassing the previous September record of 20.92°C set in 2023. Meanwhile, around Antarctica, the sea ice extent reached its third-lowest annual winter maximum,” the report said.

Copernicus is the Earth observation component of the European Union’s Space programme. It includes assistance from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) -- both as a research institute and operational service which gives global numerical weather predictions.

news.exam_corner_topic: ‘Do not put words in our mouth’: Supreme Court says it never adjudicated new Form 6, will examine challenge on Oct 27
news.headline: ‘Do not put words in our mouth’: Supreme Court says it never adjudicated new Form 6, will examine challenge on Oct 27
news.story_lead: ‘Do not put words in our mouth’: Supreme Court says it never adjudicated new Form 6, will examine challenge on Oct 27 The clarification assumes significance amid a dispute over the ECI’s claim that the Supreme Court upheld a declaration appended to Form 6 for the SIR exercise. The Supreme Court on Monday clarified that it had never adjudicated the validity of the Election Commission of India’ s (ECI) new Form 6 –– the statutory application used by citizens to register as voters, underlining that the modified version was not in existence when the court examined the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar earlier this year. The clarification assumes significance amid a dispute over the ECI’s claim that the Supreme Court upheld a declaration appended to Form 6 for the SIR exercise.
news.full_article_text: ‘Do not put words in our mouth’: Supreme Court says it never adjudicated new Form 6, will examine challenge on Oct 27 The clarification assumes significance amid a dispute over the ECI’s claim that the Supreme Court upheld a declaration appended to Form 6 for the SIR exercise. The Supreme Court on Monday clarified that it had never adjudicated the validity of the Election Commission of India’ s (ECI) new Form 6 –– the statutory application used by citizens to register as voters, underlining that the modified version was not in existence when the court examined the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar earlier this year. The clarification assumes significance amid a dispute over the ECI’s claim that the Supreme Court upheld a declaration appended to Form 6 for the SIR exercise. The court said its earlier observations could not be construed as a judicial endorsement or rejection of any modified form and agreed to examine the issue after it was brought to its notice. Also read: Rahul says INDIA bloc to move SC against CEC Gyanesh Kumar at 3pm, tells Modi ‘200 of your officers in touch with us’ ‘Do not put words in our mouth’ “Observations made by this court do not amount to constitutional adjudication. There has been no adjudication on the new Form 6 and that is all we have said,” a bench, comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, told a counsel, appearing for a fresh writ petition, on Monday. “Whether approved or not approved…that was not there. Do not put words in our mouth,” the bench added. Justice Bagchi further clarified that the CJI’s October 5 remarks only meant that the modified form did not exist when the court delivered its judgment on the Bihar SIR. “That does not say whether approved or disapproved by the Supreme Court,” he said. The bench said it would examine the issue now that it had been brought to its notice and directed that the matter be listed with the batch of petitions relating to the SIR, scheduled for October 27 when the bench will also take up a wider challenge to the functioning of ECI and the manner in which decisions concerning the electoral-roll revision exercise have been taken. Also read: Jantar Mantar in Lutyens’ Delhi de-notified as protest site; 3 new venues named What court said in earlier hearing On October 5, the bench said it had not approved any modification to Form 6 and sought records to ascertain who had authorised the changes and what they entailed. The court had issued notice on a petition challenging alleged modifications to the online form available on the ECI’s ECINet/ERONet portal. The controversy centres on an additional declaration requiring applicants to state whether their own name, or that of a parent or grandparent, appeared in the electoral roll prepared during the previous SIR. The declaration was introduced in the online registration process during the ongoing revision exercise, raising questions about its legal basis and its implications for first-time voters and those seeking to re-enter electoral rolls. What ECI said on top court's role in Form 6 changes In a September 26 press note, ECI said the Supreme Court had upheld the additional declaration, adding that the statutory Form 6 prescribed under the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, would continue to apply outside the SIR period. The Commission has maintained that the statutory form itself was not altered and that the additional declaration was an addendum specifically for the revision exercise. To be sure, ECI was likely referring to the Supreme Court’s May judgment concerning the SIR exercise in Bihar, in which the court examined the Commission’s authority to call for additional documents while revising electoral rolls. However, the additional declaration now appended to Form 6 was introduced subsequently. The 2025 ECI order on Bihar SIR referred to an Annexure D, which was a declaration form to be submitted by those filling Form 6. To be sure, that form didn’t ask for any details of an applicant’s parents’ SIR verification. These additional changes were first reported in July this year. The distinction is central to the legal challenge. Form 6 is prescribed under the 1960 rules for people seeking inclusion in electoral rolls. Under Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, the Centre frames these rules in consultation with the ECI, and changes to the rules must follow the prescribed statutory process. The petitions in the top court raise questions about whether an additional declaration could be imposed through an online form without amending the underlying rules. The requirement also has practical consequences. A young person applying to register as a voter may never have appeared in an earlier SIR roll, while applicants whose names were deleted and who seek re-enrolment may face questions about establishing the required family linkage. The legality and scope of the additional declaration therefore directly affect the process by which eligible citizens are included in electoral rolls. On October 5, senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy, appearing for advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi who has challenged the alleged changes, told the bench that two new conditions had been introduced into Form 6. The court made clear that it had not sanctioned the changes and said it wanted the underlying records before reaching any conclusion. According to an Indian Express report last month, election commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu had raised objections, arguing that Form 6 was prescribed by the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and could not be altered merely by changing the online version without following the statutory procedure. Under Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, the Centre frames the Registration of Electors Rules in consultation with the Election Commission. Amendments to the rules are required to be notified and laid before Parliament. ECI, however, has maintained that the statutory Form 6 itself was not altered and that the additional declaration was introduced specifically for the SIR exercise through an addendum. The Commission subsequently said that the additional declaration would apply only during the SIR period, while the statutory Form 6 prescribed under the 1960 rules would be used outside the exercise. The additional declaration was withdrawn from the online form in states and Union territories where the SIR exercise had been completed, with applicants there reverting to the statutory Form 6. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Utkarsh Anand Utkarsh Anand is the National Legal Editor at Hindustan Times, where he leads the newspaper's coverage of the Supreme Court, constitutional law, the judiciary and the Union law ministry. He joined Hindustan Times in 2020 after stints at Press Trust of India (PTI), The Indian Express and CNN-News18, and has over two decades of experience reporting on law, governance and public policy. To be sure, ECI was likely referring to the Supreme Court’s May judgment concerning the SIR exercise in Bihar, in which the court examined the Commission’s authority to call for additional documents while revising electoral rolls. However, the additional declaration now appended to Form 6 was introduced subsequently. The 2025 ECI order on Bihar SIR referred to an Annexure D, which was a declaration form to be submitted by those filling Form 6. To be sure, that form didn’t ask for any details of an applicant’s parents’ SIR verification. These additional changes were first reported in July this year. The distinction is central to the legal challenge. Form 6 is prescribed under the 1960 rules for people seeking inclusion in electoral rolls. Under Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, the Centre frames these rules in consultation with the ECI, and changes to the rules must follow the prescribed statutory process. The petitions in the top court raise questions about whether an additional declaration could be imposed through an online form without amending the underlying rules. The requirement also has practical consequences. A young person applying to register as a voter may never have appeared in an earlier SIR roll, while applicants whose names were deleted and who seek re-enrolment may face questions about establishing the required family linkage. The legality and scope of the additional declaration therefore directly affect the process by which eligible citizens are included in electoral rolls. On October 5, senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy, appearing for advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi who has challenged the alleged changes, told the bench that two new conditions had been introduced into Form 6. The court made clear that it had not sanctioned the changes and said it wanted the underlying records before reaching any conclusion. According to an Indian Express report last month, election commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu had raised objections, arguing that Form 6 was prescribed by the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, and could not be altered merely by changing the online version without following the statutory procedure. Under Section 28 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, the Centre frames the Registration of Electors Rules in consultation with the Election Commission. Amendments to the rules are required to be notified and laid before Parliament. ECI, however, has maintained that the statutory Form 6 itself was not altered and that the additional declaration was introduced specifically for the SIR exercise through an addendum. The Commission subsequently said that the additional declaration would apply only during the SIR period, while the statutory Form 6 prescribed under the 1960 rules would be used outside the exercise. The clarification assumes significance amid a dispute over the ECI’s claim that the Supreme Court upheld a declaration appended to Form 6 for the SIR exercise. news.story_lead: Supreme Court against blanket firecracker ban in Delhi-NCR, but asks ‘what is religious about it’ A bench comprising CJI Kant, Justice Bagchi and Justice Mohana said cooperation from citizens would be more effective in encouraging responsible celebrations The Supreme Court on Monday called for a practical approach to regulating firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, stressing that efforts to tackle air pollution must take public health concerns into account without hurting religious sentiments. The court said it was not inclined to impose a blanket ban and urged people to voluntarily adopt safer ways of celebrating. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana said public awareness and cooperation from citizens would be more effective in encouraging responsible celebrations.
news.full_article_text: Supreme Court against blanket firecracker ban in Delhi-NCR, but asks ‘what is religious about it’ A bench comprising CJI Kant, Justice Bagchi and Justice Mohana said cooperation from citizens would be more effective in encouraging responsible celebrations The Supreme Court on Monday called for a practical approach to regulating firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, stressing that efforts to tackle air pollution must take public health concerns into account without hurting religious sentiments. The court said it was not inclined to impose a blanket ban and urged people to voluntarily adopt safer ways of celebrating. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana said public awareness and cooperation from citizens would be more effective in encouraging responsible celebrations. The court was hearing suo motu proceedings concerning air pollution in Delhi-NCR, covering issues such as firecrackers, crop residue burning and solid waste management. Also Read | ‘Do not put words in our mouth’: Supreme Court says it never adjudicated new Form 6, will examine challenge on Oct 27 “We will not hurt religious sentiments, but at the same time, people should themselves come forward and opt for it. The whole exercise should involve a balancing approach. If we do that, society itself becomes awakened and people come forward. If the citizenry is concerned and civil society is aware of these things, I think that will be the best approach,” the bench said, according to Bar and Bench. What's religious about firecrackers? SC asks “What is religious about bursting of crackers,” Justice Bagchi asked. CJI Kant assured that the court would not hurt religious sentiments but urged people to voluntarily adopt safer practices. The amicus curiae also highlighted the health risks posed by air pollution, particularly to elderly people, children and those who are infirm. However, he submitted that restrictions on firecrackers were unlikely to be effective without proper enforcement. “It sounds really nice in Court, that it is only two hours or one hour. But the Court also knows that it is not implemented. It is impossible for police officers to be in every street all the time. It will not be implemented. These arguments do not work on the ground,” said the amicus. The amicus suggested that the issue be referred to the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), the statutory body responsible for air quality management in the region, which could consider the available material along with medical concerns. What CJI Kant said? CJI Kant, however, cautioned against passing restrictive orders. “We have to be extremely careful in passing an order unless we are in a position to make it manageable and enforceable,” he said. He added that restrictive orders could be perceived as coercive action and called for a practical approach to the issue. Also Read | 'Don't drag Supreme Court into politics': CJI Surya Kant amid Delhi protests row “The only problem, and we are repeating this, is that the moment you pass an order, a restrictive order, people take it as if it is a kind of coercive action. It is a human reaction. We should be very practical and pragmatic in these things. I think we have sufficient time. We should make an earnest appeal to people that they may celebrate in whatever way they want, but they should keep these two or three things in mind and restrict their celebrations to particular hours, as was done last time,” said CJI Kant. He called for greater public awareness about the harmful effects of firecrackers and suggested that the sale of highly polluting varieties could be restricted while less harmful alternatives could be permitted. “We have to make people wiser, bring awareness and tell them which firecrackers are harmful and which are less harmful. We should promote that kind of culture and persuade people to return to our original culture, where there were only sparklers and the lighting of lamps,” he said. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR HT News Desk Follow the latest breaking news, major developments and agenda-setting stories from India and around the world with the newsdesk at Hindustan Times. news.headline: India's September Inflation Nears RBI Tolerance Ceiling, Heightening Rate Hike Expectations
news.story_lead: Retail inflation in India for September registered a significant increase, coming close to the upper tolerance threshold set by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). This surge in consumer prices strengthens the argument for monetary policy tightening and potential benchmark interest rate hikes by the central bank to anchor inflationary expectations.
news.full_article_text:
### September Inflation Dynamics and Policy Implications

India's retail inflation rose sharply in September, moving close to the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) upper tolerance limit. The escalating price pressures across consumer categories have intensified concerns regarding persistent inflation, thereby bolstering the rationale for further monetary policy tightening by the central bank.

### Impact on RBI Monetary Policy

Under India's monetary policy framework, the RBI aims to maintain Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation at 4% with a statutory tolerance range of 2% to 6%. Inflation approaching the 6% upper limit restricts the central bank's policy flexibility, increasing the probability of benchmark interest rate increases in upcoming Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meetings to prevent second-round inflationary effects and maintain macroeconomic stability.
news.background_context: The Reserve Bank of India operates under a Flexible Inflation Targeting (FIT) framework mandated by the central government. The medium-term target for CPI inflation is set at 4%, with an allowable fluctuation band between 2% and 6%.
bullet_points: India's retail inflation in September approached the RBI's upper tolerance limit.
The sharp increase in consumer price levels strengthens the case for future benchmark interest rate hikes.
The RBI's statutory inflation target stands at 4% with an upper tolerance ceiling of 6%.
Accelerating inflation limits the central bank's room for monetary easing.
Higher inflation rates present a risk to consumer purchasing power and macroeconomic stability.
The monetary policy decision-making will focus on curbing inflationary pressures through prospective policy rate adjustments.

The RBI's inflation target framework is set at 4% with a 2% to 6% tolerance band.

Mains: GS Paper III (Indian Economy) - Monetary policy, inflation management, central bank interest rate mechanisms, and macroeconomic stability.
news.upsc_analysis: The uptick in inflation toward the Reserve Bank of India's upper tolerance threshold highlights the persistent macroeconomic challenge of balancing growth with price stability. When inflation approaches the 6% ceiling, monetary policy shifts toward tightening via interest rate increases, which helps anchor inflation expectations but can also impact credit flow and borrowing costs across the economy.

impacts: Heightened probability of policy interest rate hikes by the Reserve Bank of India.
Increased borrowing costs for commercial banks, businesses, and consumers.
Pressure on household purchasing power due to elevated retail prices.
challenges: Balancing inflation control through rate hikes without slowing down economic growth momentum.

hindi_translation.headline: भारत की सितंबर मुद्रास्फीति आरबीआई की सहनशीलता सीमा के करीब पहुंची, ब्याज दरों में और बढ़ोतरी की संभावना बढ़ी
hindi_translation.story_lead: सितंबर महीने में भारत की खुदरा मुद्रास्फीति में उल्लेखनीय वृद्धि दर्ज की गई, जिससे यह भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (आरबीआई) द्वारा निर्धारित सहनशीलता की ऊपरी सीमा के करीब पहुंच गई है। उपभोक्ता कीमतों में इस उछाल से मुद्रास्फीति की प्रत्याशाओं को नियंत्रित करने के लिए केंद्रीय बैंक द्वारा नीतिगत ब्याज दरों में बढ़ोतरी की संभावना मजबूत हुई है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### सितंबर मुद्रास्फीति की स्थिति और नीतिगत प्रभाव

सितंबर में भारत की खुदरा मुद्रास्फीति में तेजी से वृद्धि हुई, जो भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक (आरबीआई) की 6% की ऊपरी सहनशीलता सीमा के करीब पहुंच गई। उपभोक्ता श्रेणियों में बढ़ते मूल्य दबावों ने लगातार बनी रहने वाली महंगाई की चिंताओं को बढ़ा दिया है, जिससे केंद्रीय बैंक द्वारा सख्त मौद्रिक नीति अपनाने का आधार मजबूत हुआ है।

### आरबीआई की मौद्रिक नीति पर प्रभाव

भारत के मौद्रिक नीति ढांचे के तहत, आरबीआई का लक्ष्य उपभोक्ता मूल्य सूचकांक (CPI) आधारित मुद्रास्फीति को 4% (2% से 6% के दायरे में) बनाए रखना है। मुद्रास्फीति का 6% की ऊपरी सीमा के करीब पहुंचना केंद्रीय बैंक की नीतिगत ढील की गुंजाइश को सीमित करता है, जिससे आगामी मौद्रिक नीति समिति (MPC) की बैठकों में बेंचमार्क ब्याज दरों में बढ़ोतरी की संभावना बढ़ जाती है।
hindi_translation.background_context: भारतीय रिजर्व बैंक केंद्र सरकार द्वारा अनिवार्य फ्लेक्सिबल इन्फ्लेशन टारगेटिंग (FIT) ढांचे के तहत कार्य करता है। सीपीआई मुद्रास्फीति के लिए मध्यम अवधि का लक्ष्य 4% निर्धारित है, जिसमें 2% से 6% का उतार-चढ़ाव दायरा शामिल है।
bullet_points: सितंबर में भारत की खुदरा मुद्रास्फीति आरबीआई की सहनशीलता की ऊपरी सीमा के करीब पहुंची।
उपभोक्ता मूल्यों में तेज वृद्धि से भविष्य में नीतिगत ब्याज दर वृद्धि का मामला मजबूत हुआ है।
आरबीआई का वैधानिक मुद्रास्फीति लक्ष्य 2% से 6% के दायरा सीमा के साथ 4% निर्धारित है।
महंगाई में उछाल से केंद्रीय बैंक की मौद्रिक ढील की गुंजाइश सीमित होती है।
उच्च मुद्रास्फीति उपभोक्ता क्रय शक्ति और व्यापक आर्थिक स्थिरता के लिए जोखिम पैदा करती है।
मौद्रिक नीति संबंधी निर्णय संभावित नीतिगत दर समायोजन के माध्यम से मुद्रास्फीति को नियंत्रित करने पर केंद्रित होंगे।

आरबीआई का मुद्रास्फीति लक्ष्य ढांचा 4% (+/- 2%) निर्धारित है।

A bench of justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and NV Anjaria in its order passed on Friday said, “Having come to know of such activity happening on the ground, a suggestion has come from additional solicitor general (ASG) KM Natarj (appearing for UP government) that UGC may issue an advisory to all authorities/institutions, and especially to the public at large, not to take admission in or deal with institutions without first verifying the authenticity of such institutions. We find the suggestion to be useful, and accordingly, a direction is issued to the UGC and all the regulatory authorities to issue such a public advisory to act accordingly.” Fake medical college in Etah The fake medical college, styled as BS Medical College, operated from an old, dilapidated farmhouse and offered various courses, including D.Pharma, B.Pharma, and B.Sc. Nursing, DMLT, BMLT, BAMS, GNM and ANM. The structure had just two or three rooms and was in disrepair. No other structure appeared to be around it. These facts were brought to the court's attention by former Indian Legal Service (ILS) officer RM Sharma, who is assisting the court in a matter concerning the audit of all private universities. Sharma informed the court about a report published in a national daily regarding the fake medical college pursuant to which the police have taken action against one Satender Kumar, who is said to be running the said institution, and three other persons. During investigations, it came to light that one Bhagwan Das Singh Baghel, an illiterate tea seller, is the Chairman of the institution. When questioned, he feigned ignorance of his position. However, he admitted that he regularly signed the college documents provided by Satender Kumar. ASG Nataraj informed the court that the UP chief secretary has also ordered an independent inquiry. “We find that the same was required and that the steps taken are in the public interest so that the entire fraud on society is exposed, and based on the said inquiry, future guidelines can be issued by the UGC and all the regulatory bodies to prevent such incidents,” the court said. Even the Centre, represented by ASG Archana Pathak Dave, stated that the UGC has written to UP’s additional chief secretary, who handles the affairs of the Higher Education department, to look into the matter. The court directed the Centre to communicate its order to all regulatory bodies and monitor compliance with these directions. How the Apex Court got into the audit of private universities The issue of auditing private universities was raised in a matter where the court was considering a case filed by a student alleging that a private university harassed her when she sought to change her name in the university records. The court had appointed Sharma to examine all affidavits filed by states and union territories and make recommendations. Last month, the court directed all regulatory authorities such as the National Medical Council, National Dental Council, Indian Nursing Council, Commission for Allied and Healthcare Providers, Bar Council of India, Pharmacy Council, Veterinary Council, and National Commission for Indian System of Medicine, among others, to furnish details of their inspection of colleges relating to affiliation along with database of entire faculty and supporting staff. The bench had observed that no private university should be run as an institution for profit but rather to serve the larger public purpose of education. It sought audited accounts from every private university in the country to determine how they use their surplus income, the amounts paid to employees, and the fees collected from students under various heads. Limiting not just to finance, the court directed the universities to provide information about their admission procedure, recruitment process, actual work performed by teachers in the last year, among a host of other details that will be sent to the respective states and union territories, who will file affidavits in the top court in six weeks. The court also focused on the admission procedure and the academic quality imparted in these universities, seeking details of the person responsible for admissions, the setting of question papers, the evaluation of answer sheets, and the role of management in these functions. The order further required details of the past year's teaching hours assigned to teachers and the actual classes they taught. The matter will be heard next on November 19.

news.headline: 'Don't drag Supreme Court into politics': CJI Surya Kant amid Delhi protests row
news.story_lead: 'Don't drag Supreme Court into politics': CJI Surya Kant amid Delhi protests row Surya Kant on Monday said the Supreme Court cannot be allowed to become a “site of disruption”. Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday said the Supreme Court should not be “dragged into any politics” amid the ongoing protests against the alleged crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi, urging lawyers to ensure that the functioning of the top court and the movement of lawyers, court staff and litigants remains unhindered. “There should not be any obstruction in the functioning of the court.
news.full_article_text: 'Don't drag Supreme Court into politics': CJI Surya Kant amid Delhi protests row Surya Kant on Monday said the Supreme Court cannot be allowed to become a “site of disruption”. Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday said the Supreme Court should not be “dragged into any politics” amid the ongoing protests against the alleged crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi, urging lawyers to ensure that the functioning of the top court and the movement of lawyers, court staff and litigants remains unhindered. “There should not be any obstruction in the functioning of the court. There should not be any impediment in the movement of the lawyers, their clerks, court staff or litigants,” the CJI told Supreme Court Bar Association (SCBA) president and senior advocate Pradeep Rai, who mentioned a fresh petition concerning the detention of lawyers and the suspension of internet services. Making it clear that the court had no objection to democratic activities, CJI Kant said lawyers were free to protest but should do so at designated places. “Every member of the Bar can also protest. Wherever there is a designated place to protest, you can protest,” he told senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, who also mentioned a separate petition for listing. CJI Kant added that he had already appealed to the protesters. The observations came a day after a special bench of justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued a series of directions to protect the right to peaceful protest, restore freedom of movement and ensure that no person was detained except in accordance with the procedure established by law. The bench also directed that metro and railway services operate normally, internet connectivity remain undisturbed and restrictions around court complexes be removed to ensure access to justice. Rai sought the listing of the SCBA’s fresh petition on Tuesday, when the court is scheduled to hear the other batch of matters arising from the protests. The CJI agreed to list the plea but asked the Bar to ensure that the court’s functioning was not affected. “Alright, we will list it. But you must also see that democratic activities take place smoothly. There is no difficulty with that. But just see to it that at least the Supreme Court functioning is not affected,” said the CJI. When Rai pointed out that the lawyers were protesting peacefully, the CJI reiterated his concern about the institution being drawn into the political contest surrounding the demonstrations. “I have appealed to the protesters as well but court should not be dragged into any politics,” he said. Sankaranarayanan, who also mentioned a fresh petition relating to the police action, alleged that no order imposing prohibitory restrictions under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) was available in the public domain. He also raised concerns over the alleged detention and manhandling of senior lawyers, including Dinesh Dwivedi and Shadan Farasat. “At some point the Supreme Court will also intervene and send a strong message to the police that they cannot get away with everything,” said Sankaranarayanan, alleging that children had been hit on the head and that police personnel had taken pride in the action. The CJI, however, declined to comment further on the allegations at this stage. “I don’t want to say anything as of now,” he said, before reiterating his appeal that protests should not interfere with the court’s functioning. Senior advocate ANS Nadkarni also mentioned a fresh petition filed by a lawyer who was allegedly detained during the protests. The developments follow the Opposition’s decision to march towards the Supreme Court on Monday after the CJI declined a request by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi to meet him. The Opposition leaders had sought to apprise the CJI of their concerns over the police action against protesters, alleged irregularities in electoral processes and the functioning of constitutional institutions. The proposed meeting was declined, among other reasons, because related issues were already pending before the Supreme Court in its judicial capacity and the CJI himself had an adjudicatory role in matters concerning some of the issues raised by the Opposition. Gandhi had announced that Opposition parties, young people and civil society groups would march to the Supreme Court and seek to submit a memorandum to the CJI. The proposed march was part of a wider campaign against alleged electoral irregularities and the police crackdown on protesters demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The protests have also triggered a series of proceedings before the Supreme Court over alleged restrictions on movement, mass detentions and the curtailment of public transport ahead of Saturday’s demonstrations. On Friday, a bench led by Kant directed authorities to reconsider proposed restrictions on metro and railway services, emphasising that regulating transport was different from shutting it down. On Sunday, the special bench of justices Bagchi and Mohana issued further directions, including that peaceful, unarmed protesters could not be detained except in accordance with law. The Sunday bench also asked the authorities to explain the circumstances and manner of the alleged detentions and the legal justification for them, while issuing notices in contempt proceedings alleging non-compliance with the court’s directions against sweeping restrictions on public transport ahead of the protest called by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and other political groups demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The court is scheduled to take up the matter again on Tuesday. news.story_lead: 'Will be there': CJP backs INDIA bloc, Rahul Gandhi march to Supreme Court against CEC The Cockroach Janta Party has expressed support for Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court to raise the issue of “vote-chori”. The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) has backed INDIA bloc’s march to the Supreme Court over alleged “vote chori”, with CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka saying the organisation would participate in the protest. “All of us, all political parties and student organisations who are fighting at their own level stand in solidarity.
news.full_article_text: 'Will be there': CJP backs INDIA bloc, Rahul Gandhi march to Supreme Court against CEC The Cockroach Janta Party has expressed support for Rahul Gandhi-led INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court to raise the issue of “vote-chori”. The Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ) has backed INDIA bloc’s march to the Supreme Court over alleged “vote chori”, with CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka saying the organisation would participate in the protest. “All of us, all political parties and student organisations who are fighting at their own level stand in solidarity. Our team will be there. We hope the entire country comes together to fight this dictatorial regime,” Ranka told reporters. Opposition parties led by Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi are scheduled to march ‘peacefully’ to the Supreme Court at 1.30 pm and submit a memorandum to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant over the alleged electoral malpractice. Rahul Gandhi and Rajya Sabha Leader of Opposition Mallikarjun Kharge have sought a meeting with Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to raise allegations of “vote chori”. However, the CJI declined to meet Gandhi over the allegations. Gandhi has also called for a news conference on the protest. In a post on X he said, "March for Democracy. March for Justice. Chalo Dilli." Also Read: ' Tell us in 24 hours or we will': CJP's ultimatum over Jantar Mantar protest amid access restrictions CJP's ultimatum to Delhi police Ranka on Monday gave the Delhi Police 24 hours to provide a date for a protest at Jantar Mantar, warning that the party would announce its next course of action if it did not receive a response within the deadline. Ranka and fellow co-convener Saurav Dass visited the Parliament Street police station to press for a date. “Jantar Mantar is the designated protest site and we are here to seek dates on which we can carry out our protest,” Ranka said. “Where should I carry out our protest? They should tell us in the next 24 hours how we can proceed with the protest. Otherwise, we will give our next call,” he added. CJP co-convener Saurav Das said the party was willing to let the police decide the date and time of the protest. “Police tells everyone to approach them 10 days in advance. We are now saying that they have the choice to tell us the date and time (for protest at Jantar Mantar). We are giving them 24-hour ultimatum,” Das said. Security beefed up in Central Delhi High Security is in place in Central Delhi as the INDIA bloc is set to lead a protest march to the Supreme Court. Security has been tightened with barricades at multiple locations, and entry and exit at certain metro stations will remain closed from 6:00 AM to 4:00 PM on October 12, 2026, for security reasons. Security personnel have been deployed at Barakhamba Road, near Mandi House. RAF (Rapid Action Force) and CRPF (Central Reserve Police Force) personnel are also deployed along with Delhi Police personnel. news.exam_corner_topic: Appointment Process of Election Commission of India
static_gk: The Election Commission of India (ECI) is an autonomous constitutional authority established under Article 324 of the Constitution of India.
The ECI was established on January 25, 1950, a day celebrated as National Voters' Day.
The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) are appointed by the President of India.
news.headline: Appointments in the Election Commission of India: Understanding the Legal Framework and Process
news.story_lead: The procedure for appointing the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners is a fundamental aspect of India's democratic structure. The mechanism ensures the independent functioning of the Election Commission of India in conducting free and fair elections.
news.full_article_text:
### Overview of ECI Appointments

The Election Commission of India (ECI) operates as a constitutional body responsible for administering election processes in India at the national and state levels. Under Article 324 of the Indian Constitution, the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections is vested in the Commission.

### Key Aspects of the Appointment Process
* **Constitutional Provision:** Article 324(2) specifies that the Election Commission shall consist of the Chief Election Commissioner and such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may fix from time to time.
* **Appointing Authority:** Appointments to the Election Commission are made by the President of India.
* **Institutional Independence:** The independence of the Commission is safeguarded to ensure impartial conduct of elections across the country.
bullet_points: Article 324 of the Indian Constitution governs the structure and function of the Election Commission of India.
Appointments of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners are executed by the President.
The structure of the Commission can consist of a Chief Election Commissioner and additional Commissioners as determined by the President.
The ECI is tasked with directing, controlling, and conducting elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, and the offices of President and Vice-President.
Constitutional safeguards are provided to maintain institutional autonomy and administrative neutrality.

hindi_translation.story_lead: भारत के मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त और निर्वाचन आयुक्तों की नियुक्ति प्रक्रिया भारत के लोकतांत्रिक ढांचे का एक महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा है। यह व्यवस्था स्वतंत्र और निष्पक्ष चुनाव कराने के लिए निर्वाचन आयोग की स्वतंत्र कार्यप्रणाली सुनिश्चित करती है।
hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### निर्वाचन आयोग की नियुक्तियों का विवरण

भारत निर्वाचन आयोग (ECI) एक संवैधानिक निकाय है जो राष्ट्रीय और राज्य स्तर पर चुनाव प्रक्रियाओं का संचालन करता है। भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 324 के तहत, चुनावों के अधीक्षण, निर्देशन और नियंत्रण की शक्ति आयोग में निहित है।

### नियुक्ति प्रक्रिया के प्रमुख बिंदु
* **संवैधानिक प्रावधान:** अनुच्छेद 324(2) में निर्दिष्ट है कि निर्वाचन आयोग में मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त और ऐसे अन्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त शामिल होंगे, जिन्हें राष्ट्रपति समय-समय पर नियत करें।
* **नियुक्ति प्राधिकारी:** निर्वाचन आयोग में नियुक्तियां भारत के राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती हैं।
* **संस्थागत स्वतंत्रता:** देश भर में निष्पक्ष चुनाव संचालन सुनिश्चित करने के लिए आयोग की स्वतंत्रता की रक्षा की जाती है।
bullet_points: भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 324 भारत निर्वाचन आयोग की संरचना और कार्यों का संचालन करता है।
मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त और निर्वाचन आयुक्तों की नियुक्तियां राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती हैं।
आयोग की संरचना में एक मुख्य निर्वाचन आयुक्त और राष्ट्रपति द्वारा तय किए गए अतिरिक्त आयुक्त शामिल हो सकते हैं।
ECI को संसद, राज्य विधानमंडलों, राष्ट्रपति और उपराष्ट्रपति के पदों के चुनावों का निर्देशन और नियंत्रण करने का दायित्व सौंपा गया है।

news.headline: Orangutans released back into Borneo forest after devastating fires
news.story_lead: Watch: Endangered orangutans released back into the wild after after Borneo fires - Published 5 hours ago Eight orangutans have been released back into the wild in Borneo after they were taken into captivity when their habitat was threatened by wildfires over the summer. Three mothers, their three daughters and two adult males were freed in a reserve in the west of the island on Friday, International Animal Rescue Indonesia (Yiari) and the forestry ministry said. Indonesian authorities rescued 46 orangutans from fires in August and September.
news.full_article_text: Watch: Endangered orangutans released back into the wild after after Borneo fires - Published 5 hours ago Eight orangutans have been released back into the wild in Borneo after they were taken into captivity when their habitat was threatened by wildfires over the summer. Three mothers, their three daughters and two adult males were freed in a reserve in the west of the island on Friday, International Animal Rescue Indonesia (Yiari) and the forestry ministry said. Indonesian authorities rescued 46 orangutans from fires in August and September. Wildfires in the region are usual for the country's dry season but intensified this year. The apes are critically endangered. Around 104,000 orangutans remain in Borneo and Sumatra, down from more than 230,000 a century ago, according to conservation group WWF. While Indonesia is among many countries to grapple with wildfires each summer, this year's were more intense due to the El NiÃ±o ocean warming phenomenon, which makes weather patterns more volatile and intense. Yiari CEO Karmele Llano Sanchez said relocating the eight orangutans to the reserve was a "necessary step" when their habitats became unsafe. Among them was Mama Nopi and her offspring Nopi, Naufal and Nopan, who had been surviving in a coconut and rubber plantation before their rescue in early September, Yiari said. Fires had incinerated the surrounding forestry, restricting their access to food and bringing them closer to humans. The apes were all rescued from wildfires over the summer that threatened their habitats Mama Lifa and her child Lifa were found in a patch of acacia trees entirely surrounded by oil palm plantations. The degradation of their habitat by wildfires as well as a lack of food sources prompted their rescue in mid-September. Mama Man and her baby, Man, had been monitored by animal rescuers since June, when they were found living in a plantation area adjacent to a small patch of forest. Fires that spread near to the site restricted their roaming area further, leaving them without a safe route to other forestry. The threat of exposure to the blazes led to them being evacuated in early September, Yiara said. The reserve these orangutans were released into was chosen because it there is food and water available and it is connected to other forested areas. Yiari's Argitoe Ranting said: "We want to ensure that rescued orangutans are not simply moved from one place to another, but actually have a chance to survive in their natural habitat." The orangutans were moved to a reserve connected with other forests and with plenty of natural resources Last month, the International Union for Conservation of Nature warned that wildfires were burning in habitats containing 52% of Borneo's orangutan population. It says a large portion of the ape's habitat will become inhospitable to them if climate change continues at its current pace. This year's El NiÃ±o has become the strongest on record and is expected to have a knock-on effect on the climate into next year. Experts have also pointed to land-clearing practices used to make room for plantations as another factor facilitating the spread of wildfires in Indonesia, with naturally fire-resistant forests replaced by less dense and shaded vegetation. That the orangutan's original habitats had been burned and fragmented to the point they could no longer sustain the primates was the main driving factor behind relocating them, Yiara said. सऊदी अरब स्थित एक हवाई अड्डे पर मिसाइल हमले के दौरान एक भारतीय नागरिक की मौत हो गई। उपलब्ध जानकारी के अनुसार, इस हमले में उनके दो बेटे भी घायल हो गए और उन्हें बाद में अस्पताल में भर्ती कराया गया।

इस हमले के परिणामस्वरूप स्थल पर ही भारतीय नागरिक की मृत्यु हो गई, जबकि उनके दो बेटों का स्थानीय अस्पताल में इलाज जारी है। यह घटना क्षेत्र में मौजूद विदेशी नागरिकों की सुरक्षा से जुड़ी चिंताओं को रेखांकित करती है।

news.headline: 'Would not see such a fast mutation even in radioactive decay': BJP hits out at CJP amid protests against CEC
news.story_lead: 'Would not see such a fast mutation even in radioactive decay': BJP hits out at CJP amid protests against CEC Top CJP leaders on Sunday vowed to expand their protests over alleged irregularities during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The BJP on Sunday took on the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), saying the group, which cropped up just months ago and led an agitation over the alleged NEET paper leak and primarily students' concerns, has "suddenly" shifted its focus to an issue related to electoral politics. "Perhaps you wouldn't see such a fast mutation (change) even in radioactive decay," BJP Rajya Sabha MP Sudhanshu Trivedi jibed, while replying to media queries during a press conference at the BJP headquarters here.
news.full_article_text: 'Would not see such a fast mutation even in radioactive decay': BJP hits out at CJP amid protests against CEC Top CJP leaders on Sunday vowed to expand their protests over alleged irregularities during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Follow live updates on the CJP protest here . On Saturday, senior BJP leader Ravi Shakar Prasad had alleged that CJP is doing "shadow-boxing" for the Aam Aadmi Party. Top CJP leaders on Sunday vowed to expand their protests over alleged irregularities during Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, who were set free on a condition that they would not "breach peace" for a year, claimed their detention was illegal and the protest would continue till Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Also Read | Abhijeet Dipke, team CJP released by court after detention, but on one condition Asked about the CJP leaders vowing to continue their protest, Trivedi said, "Look, everyone has the right to protest, but how much it is accepted thereafter is a different matter altogether." "Another thing has also become clear; what was a students' movement over the examination system, just two months ago, has suddenly turned into agitation over electoral issues," he said in a guarded response. "Perhaps you wouldn't see such a fast mutation even in radioactive decay," he jibed, reiterating, "But, everyone has the right. Whoever wants to protest may protest," Also Read | SC to take up pleas against detentions during CJP protest, curbs on transport Trivedi said the recent victory of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) in various campus polls reflects students' sentiments and the ground reality. "We have won the Delhi University students' union elections. We have won the Panjab University student union elections as well. The sentiment of the youth is clearly visible on the ground," he added. The CJP had led a protest at Jantar Mantar over the NEET paper leak issue in June-July, which culminated in the resignation of erstwhile Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. - Cockroach Janta Party - Special Intensive Revision Sir

news.headline: Sachin Pilot may even deny me ticket; will always remain Rahul Gandhi’s soldier: Warring
news.story_lead: Sachin Pilot may even deny me ticket; will always remain Rahul Gandhi’s soldier: Warring Warring quit as the Punjab Congress chief on October 1, after the Congress high command decided on a leadership change ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Days after quitting as the Punjab Congress president, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Sunday said he may have "lost or fallen", or AICC's Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot may even deny him a ticket for next year's Assembly elections, yet he would continue to hold the Congress flag high as a soldier of Rahul Gandhi. The Ludhiana MP also acknowledged that many in the party opposed him when he was the Punjab Congress president, and that they may continue to do so – remarks seen as directed at his detractors in the state unit.
news.full_article_text: Sachin Pilot may even deny me ticket; will always remain Rahul Gandhi’s soldier: Warring Warring quit as the Punjab Congress chief on October 1, after the Congress high command decided on a leadership change ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Days after quitting as the Punjab Congress president, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Sunday said he may have "lost or fallen", or AICC's Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot may even deny him a ticket for next year's Assembly elections, yet he would continue to hold the Congress flag high as a soldier of Rahul Gandhi. The Ludhiana MP also acknowledged that many in the party opposed him when he was the Punjab Congress president, and that they may continue to do so – remarks seen as directed at his detractors in the state unit. Warring, however, said he will fully support new Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh, who on Sunday took charge of his new post at a ceremony held at the Congress Bhavan that was attended by Pilot, among others. Ahead of the ceremony, Warring held a gathering at a rented house in Sector 10, close to the party headquarters in Sector 15, where Congress leaders Brahm Mohindra, Rana K P Singh, Surinder Dawar, Anil Joshi, Simarjit Singh Bains, Hardyal Kamboj, Malvika Sood and his supporters were present. The gathering was seen as a show of strength by Warring. Amid an intense race for the top organisational post, with former Sangrur MP Vijay Inder Singla seen as a frontrunner, the party named ex-India hockey captain and three-time Jalandhar Cantt MLA Pargat Singh (61) as the new state unit chief the next day. The move followed weeks of internal unrest over the state leadership that threatened to hurt the party's campaign for the Assembly elections due early next year. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Warring said the Congress is united in its quest to form the next government in Punjab. "There is no other objective. Raja Warring may have lost and fallen, but my job is to keep holding the party flag high," Warring said. Later during his address at the Congress Bhavan with Pilot in attendance, Warring stressed that he was a soldier of Rahul Gandhi. "No doubt many people opposed Raja Warring, and they may continue to do so. But I am not opposing anyone," he said. Hinting at his resignation, Warring said Pilot was here and "I myself had said I have lost". "I only consider Rahul Gandhi as my leader," he said, adding that the Congress gave a lot to him. "If I say that I would remain the president and only what I say should be heard, it won't be right," Warring said. In an apparent dig at Pilot, Warring said, "Pilot Saab may cut my ticket next time. But I will continue to remain a soldier of Rahul Gandhi and will always be with the Congress." After the party decided to replace him on October 2, Warring had said he came to know that Pilot wanted him replaced, but he "voluntarily" relinquished his charge. On Sunday, Warring said he would continue to support whoever the party makes the president. Referring to his recent meeting with Rahul Gandhi, Warring said he urged the senior party leader to allot more than 50 per cent tickets to the youth fighting the party's battle. Before the ceremony, Warring said, "I had maintained that whosoever becomes the (Punjab Congress) president, I would be with him. Be it Pargat Singh or Charanjit Singh Channi." However, he added that Channi did not want to go along with him. Warring was replaced as the Punjab Congress chief weeks after Pilot took charge as the general secretary in charge of Punjab. A section of leaders led by Channi had opposed a move to retain Warring as the state unit president and sought his removal from the post.

hindi_translation.full_article_text: Sachin Pilot may even deny me ticket; will always remain Rahul Gandhi’s soldier: Warring Warring quit as the Punjab Congress chief on October 1, after the Congress high command decided on a leadership change ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Days after quitting as the Punjab Congress president, Amrinder Singh Raja Warring on Sunday said he may have "lost or fallen", or AICC's Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot may even deny him a ticket for next year's Assembly elections, yet he would continue to hold the Congress flag high as a soldier of Rahul Gandhi. The Ludhiana MP also acknowledged that many in the party opposed him when he was the Punjab Congress president, and that they may continue to do so – remarks seen as directed at his detractors in the state unit. Warring, however, said he will fully support new Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh, who on Sunday took charge of his new post at a ceremony held at the Congress Bhavan that was attended by Pilot, among others. Ahead of the ceremony, Warring held a gathering at a rented house in Sector 10, close to the party headquarters in Sector 15, where Congress leaders Brahm Mohindra, Rana K P Singh, Surinder Dawar, Anil Joshi, Simarjit Singh Bains, Hardyal Kamboj, Malvika Sood and his supporters were present. The gathering was seen as a show of strength by Warring. Amid an intense race for the top organisational post, with former Sangrur MP Vijay Inder Singla seen as a frontrunner, the party named ex-India hockey captain and three-time Jalandhar Cantt MLA Pargat Singh (61) as the new state unit chief the next day. The move followed weeks of internal unrest over the state leadership that threatened to hurt the party's campaign for the Assembly elections due early next year. Speaking to reporters on Sunday, Warring said the Congress is united in its quest to form the next government in Punjab. "There is no other objective. Raja Warring may have lost and fallen, but my job is to keep holding the party flag high," Warring said. Later during his address at the Congress Bhavan with Pilot in attendance, Warring stressed that he was a soldier of Rahul Gandhi. "No doubt many people opposed Raja Warring, and they may continue to do so. But I am not opposing anyone," he said. Hinting at his resignation, Warring said Pilot was here and "I myself had said I have lost". "I only consider Rahul Gandhi as my leader," he said, adding that the Congress gave a lot to him. "If I say that I would remain the president and only what I say should be heard, it won't be right," Warring said. In an apparent dig at Pilot, Warring said, "Pilot Saab may cut my ticket next time. But I will continue to remain a soldier of Rahul Gandhi and will always be with the Congress." After the party decided to replace him on October 2, Warring had said he came to know that Pilot wanted him replaced, but he "voluntarily" relinquished his charge. On Sunday, Warring said he would continue to support whoever the party makes the president. Referring to his recent meeting with Rahul Gandhi, Warring said he urged the senior party leader to allot more than 50 per cent tickets to the youth fighting the party's battle. Before the ceremony, Warring said, "I had maintained that whosoever becomes the (Punjab Congress) president, I would be with him. Be it Pargat Singh or Charanjit Singh Channi." However, he added that Channi did not want to go along with him. Warring was replaced as the Punjab Congress chief weeks after Pilot took charge as the general secretary in charge of Punjab. A section of leaders led by Channi had opposed a move to retain Warring as the state unit president and sought his removal from the post.

news.headline: Indian killed in Riyadh airport attack on October 10; MEA condemns Houthi strikes
news.story_lead: Indian killed in Riyadh airport attack on October 10; MEA condemns Houthi strikes The embassy said it was in touch with Saudi authorities to inquire about the well-being of the injured Indians. India on Sunday strongly condemned repeated attacks by Houthi rebels on the international airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital, including the latest strike that killed 13 people, including an Indian, and called for an immediate end to the targeting of civilian infrastructure across the region. Track live updates on Saudi-Houthi war Initial reports following Saturday's attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh said 12 people were killed and 309 others injured.
news.full_article_text: Indian killed in Riyadh airport attack on October 10; MEA condemns Houthi strikes The embassy said it was in touch with Saudi authorities to inquire about the well-being of the injured Indians. India on Sunday strongly condemned repeated attacks by Houthi rebels on the international airport in Saudi Arabia’s capital, including the latest strike that killed 13 people, including an Indian, and called for an immediate end to the targeting of civilian infrastructure across the region. Track live updates on Saudi-Houthi war Initial reports following Saturday's attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh said 12 people were killed and 309 others injured. The Indian embassy in Riyadh said on social media late on Sunday night that one of 11 Indian nationals injured in the attack had “unfortunately lost his life”. “Deeply grieved at the loss of life of an Indian national in the Riyadh attack. My heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family. The Embassy will extend all possible assistance,” external affairs minister S Jaishankar said on social media. Also read: ‘Deeply grieved’: Jaishankar assures all assistance to family of Indian killed in Riyadh attack The Indian side expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia in the defence of the country’s sovereignty against the backdrop of an escalation in attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels as the war in West Asia expands. This was the third attack on the King Khalid international airport over the past week. “We strongly condemn the repeated attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack on October 10, which have led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property,” the external affairs ministry said in a statement that did not name anyone for the attacks. “We stand in solidarity with the people and the government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy returns to the region at the earliest,” the statement said. Also read: Riyadh airport ops halted, Houthis' fresh warning: Major escalation after latest strike kills 12 in Saudi The Indian embassy in Riyadh said it was in touch with Saudi authorities to ensure the well-being of injured Indians. The external affairs ministry statement described the repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure as “completely unacceptable” and said they “must cease immediately”. The Indian side expressed condolences to the families of the dead and wished for the speedy recovery of the injured. Nearly 20 Indians have died so far in the West Asia conflict, which began in February. Deep Dive Saudi Arabia is home to more than four million Indians, one of the largest concentrations of the diaspora in West Asia. Saturday’s attack on the airport was the deadliest in Saudi Arabia in more than a decade, as the Houthis escalated a campaign they launched in summer. The dead included four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshis and one national each from Egypt, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and the US, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. Two earlier attacks on the same airport last week killed four people and caused extensive damage to a Saudi commercial plane. The strikes also exposed vulnerabilities in Saudi Arabia’s defence capabilities as the kingdom wages an air campaign against the Houthis to support a ground war by the Yemeni government against the group. President Donald Trump said the US is considering joining Saudi strikes on Houthis in the conflict, a spillover from the war on Iran that the US and Israel started in February. Saudi Arabia entered the war in Yemen in 2015 at the head of a coalition that aimed to force the Houthis out of the Yemeni capital Sanaa. The war turned into a stalemate, with hundreds of thousands of Yemenis killed by fighting and famine. A 2022 ceasefire by the Saudis and the Houthis unravelled this summer, culminating in a sudden Houthi advance that took the Red Sea chokepoint of Bab el-Mandeb from Saudi-backed government forces. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Rezaul H Laskar Rezaul Hasan Laskar is Foreign Editor with the Hindustan Times, which he joined in 2015. He began as a journalist in his hometown of Shillong in northeast India and has worked in newspapers and wire services over the years. He moved to New Delhi in 1997 and initially focused on defence, national security, Jammu and Kashmir and the northeast, while also working of foreign policy and international relations. He has been part of the media delegation accompanying PMs on foreign visits and has reported from destinations ranging from Tibet to Ukraine. Between 2007 and 2013, he was the Press Trust of India correspondent in Pakistan, one of only two Indian journalists allowed to report from the country. He extensively covered Pakistan’s domestic politics and the life of the common people, as well as the fallout of the 2008 Mumbai attacks on India-Pakistan relations and the subsequent trial in Pakistan of the suspects involved in the attack. As part of his reportage in Pakistan, he travelled the breadth of the country, from the Swat Valley to Balochistan. Reza’s first gig in journalism was writing a weekly music column, and music – especially classic rock – remains a keen interest. He is also a movie buff and a keen photographer. Read More

news.headline: ‘Detain, deport foreign citizen Imran Khan': BJP leader Kirit Somaiya writes to Mumbai Police after actor joins protest
news.story_lead: ‘Detain, deport foreign citizen Imran Khan': BJP leader Kirit Somaiya writes to Mumbai Police after actor joins protest Somaiya called for Khan to be charged for participating in what he described as an illegal political agitation. BJP leader Kirit Somaiya has urged the Mumbai Police to take action against actor Imran Khan for joining a protest in support of the Cockroach Janta Party, citing his alleged status as a “foreign citizen”. Calling for Khan's detention and deportation, the BJP leader also sought clarity on whether the actor could participate in such protests.
news.full_article_text: ‘Detain, deport foreign citizen Imran Khan': BJP leader Kirit Somaiya writes to Mumbai Police after actor joins protest Somaiya called for Khan to be charged for participating in what he described as an illegal political agitation. BJP leader Kirit Somaiya has urged the Mumbai Police to take action against actor Imran Khan for joining a protest in support of the Cockroach Janta Party, citing his alleged status as a “foreign citizen”. Calling for Khan's detention and deportation, the BJP leader also sought clarity on whether the actor could participate in such protests. In a post on X, Somaiya said he had written to Mumbai Police Joint Commissioner Manoj Kumar Sharma, asking whether Khan, a “foreign citizen”, could “break the law knowingly”. Somaiya called for Khan to be charged for participating in what he described as an illegal political agitation, alleging violations of OCI provisions and visa conditions. He argued that foreign citizens do not enjoy the same rights as Indian citizens. Deep Dive He also demanded Khan’s immediate deportation. Khan was detained by the Mumbai Police on October 10 from Mumbai's August Kranti Maidan, which was the proposed protest venue in support of CJP’s protest call. The actor took to Instagram and shared a selfie from inside the police van. “Apparently I’m going for a drive,” he said in the caption. Speaking to the media on Saturday, Khan clarified that he was not present with any specific demands but had come forward in his capacity as a citizen of Mumbai. He said he wanted to understand why freedom of movement was being restricted and why people’s voices were being suppressed. “I don't have demands. I am here as a citizen, as a person who lives in this city. I am here to see why freedom of movement is being restricted. Why are people's voices being suppressed? That is why I am here,” the actor said. More than 400 people were detained on Saturday for protesting at August Kranti Maidan in support of the CJP, according to the Mumbai Police. Mumbai Police said no permission had been sought for the protest in support of the CJP. They also said they could not grant permission, as the Bombay high court’s directions allow protests to be held only at Azad Maidan. However, CJP workers claimed they had emailed the Mumbai Police seeking permission but had received no response. The gathering was called by Tushar Gandhi, great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, in support of the CJP's demand for the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar amid a row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Tushar Gandhi was detained while heading towards the site and was later released by the Mumbai Police. - ABOUT THE AUTHOR Karishma Ayaldasani Karishma Ayaldasani is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times, based in New Delhi, where she works with the digital team on fast-moving breaking stories from India and around the world. Comfortable in high-pressure newsroom settings, she regularly contributes to live blogs, explainers and real-time coverage. Outside of work, she likes exploring different art forms and unwinds with music.
