news.headline: CJI Surya Kant declines Opposition leaders' request for meet over SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar; cites judicial propriety
news.story_lead: CJI Surya Kant declines Opposition leaders' request for meet over SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar; cites judicial propriety The Opposition’s proposed intervention also comes amid its continuing campaign against the SIR exercise and allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls. The Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has declined a request by Opposition leaders to meet him on Monday, citing extensive reasons why such an interaction would not be appropriate at this juncture and in the present circumstances, dealing a setback to the Opposition’s plan to seek his intervention over the crackdown on a youth-led protest in Delhi and alleged irregularities in electoral processes. Among the key reasons cited were the pendency of related matters before the Supreme Court in its judicial capacity and the CJI’s own adjudicatory role in petitions concerning these issues, people aware of the matter said
news.full_article_text: CJI Surya Kant declines Opposition leaders' request for meet over SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar; cites judicial propriety The Opposition’s proposed intervention also comes amid its continuing campaign against the SIR exercise and allegations of irregularities in electoral rolls. The Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has declined a request by Opposition leaders to meet him on Monday, citing extensive reasons why such an interaction would not be appropriate at this juncture and in the present circumstances, dealing a setback to the Opposition’s plan to seek his intervention over the crackdown on a youth-led protest in Delhi and alleged irregularities in electoral processes. Among the key reasons cited were the pendency of related matters before the Supreme Court in its judicial capacity and the CJI’s own adjudicatory role in petitions concerning these issues, people aware of the matter said. Also Read | Opposition march to Supreme Court tomorrow; leaders seek to meet CJI against SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar Opposition's meeting with CJI Deep Dive The decision came hours after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi announced that they had sought time to meet the CJI between 4 pm and 5 pm on Monday. Kharge had said that he and Gandhi had written to the CJI, seeking an opportunity to apprise him of their concerns over the functioning of constitutional institutions and request his intervention. The Opposition had planned to raise several issues, including the police action against protesters demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the expeditious hearing of cases concerning the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and the composition of the committee that recommends appointments to the Election Commission. The proposed meeting had not been confirmed by the CJI’s office when the Opposition announced its plans on Sunday. Kharge, speaking to reporters in Bengaluru, had said the delegation would place its concerns before the CJI with folded hands, adding that the leaders could not make demands of the head of the judiciary. news.headline: Maharashtra govt to submit detailed memorandum for Central drought relief
news.story_lead: Maharashtra govt to submit detailed memorandum for Central drought relief Mumbai, Oct 11 Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday said the state government is undertaking detailed planning to provide employment, foodgrains, drinking water and fodder for livestock in drought-affected areas over the next six to eight months. At a meeting with a Central drought assessment team at his official residence here, Fadnavis said deficient rainfall during a crucial stage of crop growth had severely affected soybean cultivation in several areas, while cotton, tur and sugarcane crops had also suffered damage. The prospects for rabi sowing are bleak due to water shortages, leaving farmers with little scope to make up for their kharif crop losses through subsequent cultivation, he said.
news.full_article_text: Maharashtra govt to submit detailed memorandum for Central drought relief Mumbai, Oct 11 Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis on Sunday said the state government is undertaking detailed planning to provide employment, foodgrains, drinking water and fodder for livestock in drought-affected areas over the next six to eight months. At a meeting with a Central drought assessment team at his official residence here, Fadnavis said deficient rainfall during a crucial stage of crop growth had severely affected soybean cultivation in several areas, while cotton, tur and sugarcane crops had also suffered damage. The prospects for rabi sowing are bleak due to water shortages, leaving farmers with little scope to make up for their kharif crop losses through subsequent cultivation, he said. Small farmers dependent on agricultural labour for livelihood are facing economic hardship, and the government will provide assistance through employment generation and food security schemes, Fadnavis said. He expressed confidence that the Central team, which visited drought-affected villages and interacted with farmers, would submit a report highlighting the severity of the situation to the Union government. "Water sources have dried up in several parts of Maharashtra, particularly in small rural villages, necessitating extensive arrangements for tanker-based supply. The state government is planning to use technology to ensure transparent and systematic distribution of water through tankers," he said. Fadnavis said drinking water requirements of people and livestock will be prioritised, with available water reserved for drinking purposes until August 2027. Water for other uses would be made available only after these requirements were met, he added. "The government will also undertake desilting, repairs and rejuvenation of water storage structures under various Central and state schemes. Works in 25,000 villages had earlier provided relief even when the water deficit was between 15 and 17 per cent," Fadnavis said, adding that software and mobile applications would be used to ensure transparency in implementation. The available fodder stock in various districts is estimated to last 90 to 120 days, the chief minister said, adding that production will be increased in watershed areas with adequate soil moisture. He said the government would procure fodder at declared rates and arrange for its storage. "Procurement from other states with better rainfall would also be considered if necessary," he said, adding that fodder and cattle camps will be set up wherever required, while water conservation works will be undertaken with public participation to generate employment in rural areas. He said the state government will submit a detailed memorandum, supported by data and prepared in accordance with the Union government's norms, to seek drought relief. "An advance memorandum had already been submitted following communication from the Union Agriculture Minister," Fadnavis said. He added that the Union Home Minister had assured the state that a meeting of an inter-ministerial group would be convened soon to expedite the relief process. The state government will also coordinate with the Centre to ensure that farmers covered by crop insurance received their benefits at the earliest, he said. The meeting was attended by Disaster Management Minister Girish Mahajan, Agriculture Minister Dattatray Bharne, Relief and Rehabilitation Minister Makarand Jadhav Patil, and Central team head and Joint Secretary Muktanand Agrawal, among others. Three teams of Central government officials visited agricultural fields and water sources in drought-affected villages across Ahilyanagar, Solapur, Jalna, Beed, Dharashiv, Washim and Yavatmal districts to assess the situation and interact with farmers. He expressed confidence that the Central team, which visited drought-affected villages and interacted with farmers, would submit a report highlighting the severity of the situation to the Union government.

news.exam_corner_topic: Opposition march to Supreme Court tomorrow; leaders seek to meet CJI against SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar
news.headline: Opposition march to Supreme Court tomorrow; leaders seek to meet CJI against SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar
news.story_lead: Opposition march to Supreme Court tomorrow; leaders seek to meet CJI against SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, who was absent from the previous two marches, will join the INDIA bloc’s march tomorrow. Opposition leaders will march from Connaught Place to the Supreme Court to meet Chief Justice of India Surya Kant after 4 pm on Monday to raise the "vote chori" issue. Opposition parties have urged people to join their next round of protests on Monday that will include an unprecedented march to the Supreme Court after security forces turned central Delhi into a fortress and clamped down on thousands of protesters to stop a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led movement demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
news.full_article_text: Opposition march to Supreme Court tomorrow; leaders seek to meet CJI against SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, who was absent from the previous two marches, will join the INDIA bloc’s march tomorrow. Opposition leaders will march from Connaught Place to the Supreme Court to meet Chief Justice of India Surya Kant after 4 pm on Monday to raise the "vote chori" issue. Opposition parties have urged people to join their next round of protests on Monday that will include an unprecedented march to the Supreme Court after security forces turned central Delhi into a fortress and clamped down on thousands of protesters to stop a Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led movement demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Congress general secretary K C Venugopal said, “We appeal to every Indian concerned about the survival of Indian democracy to join us in a massive protest march in Delhi on Monday - against the nationwide Vote Chori orchestrated by the Modi-Shah regime.” Venugopal, one of the key strategists behind the Opposition’s protest plans, added, “INDIA MPs, leaders, workers and all concerned citizens will be holding a huge protest march against Gyanesh & Co, and a delegation of our senior leaders will submit a memorandum to the Hon’ble CJI for his intervention in this crisis.” ‘Daro mat', says Rahul Gandhi ahead of march to SC Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said the Opposition would march to the Supreme Court and submit a memorandum to the Chief Justice on behalf of the nation, demanding an end to “vote chori”, a halt to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. “We will march to the Supreme Court as Indians, united beyond party, gender, caste, community and state. Youth, all opposition parties, civil society groups, all those who believe in democracy and stand by the Constitution of India, will walk with us,” he wrote in a post on X. “Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Ajit Doval and Mohan Bhagwat cannot silence India's voice. These cowards cannot intimidate us. They will have to step aside. We will march together, with love, brotherhood and patriotism. “Daro mat. Tomorrow, all of India will march to the Supreme Court,” he added. Gandhi also criticised the treatment of protesters at Jantar Mantar on Saturday, alleging that they had been beaten despite gathering for a peaceful demonstration. “Yesterday, the nation's young came out in Delhi to peacefully protest. They came with love in their hearts, not hatred or anger. They were beaten, both by cops and BJP goons. This is not the India we want,” he wrote. news.story_lead: CJP leaders to visit Delhi's Parliament Street Police Station tomorrow, seek date for fresh Jantar Mantar protest CJP leaders said the Delhi Police have 24 hours to provide them with a date for the protest Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders, including Saurav Das , will visit the Parliamentary Street Police Station at 10 am on Monday to seek a date for holding a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. In a statement, the leaders said the Delhi Police had 24 hours to provide them with a date for the protest, failing which they would announce a protest call themselves. news.full_article_text: CJP leaders to visit Delhi's Parliament Street Police Station tomorrow, seek date for fresh Jantar Mantar protest CJP leaders said the Delhi Police have 24 hours to provide them with a date for the protest Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) leaders, including Saurav Das , will visit the Parliamentary Street Police Station at 10 am on Monday to seek a date for holding a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. In a statement, the leaders said the Delhi Police had 24 hours to provide them with a date for the protest, failing which they would announce a protest call themselves. Also Read | Detentions continue in Delhi despite Supreme Court order, 100 held from Connaught Place "CJP leaders will go to Parliament Street police station at 10 am on Monday to seek date for peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar, says Ashutosh Ranka. On Saturday, CJP leaders, including Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, were detained amid a major security clampdown, with more than 7,000 protesters detained at multiple locations as police prevented them from reaching Jantar Mantar. Over the past two days, CJP leaders were detained and subsequently released by the Delhi Police following a court order. Protesters, including All India Students' Association (AISA) leader Neha Bora, continued their demonstrations on Sunday but were also detained and later released. Ranka and Das came down heavily on the Centre at their first press conference after coming out of 24-hour detention by the Delhi Police. Das said the entire country was in an emergency-like situation, with protesters being detained, transport curbs in place and internet services shut down in parts of the national capital. Also Read | Opposition march to Supreme Court tomorrow; leaders seek to meet CJI against SIR, CEC Gyanesh Kumar The Supreme Court, during a special sitting on Sunday, ruled that peaceful, unarmed protesters cannot be detained except in accordance with the “procedure established by law”. However, the Delhi Police continued to detain protesters around Connaught Place on Sunday, including CPI(M) leader John Brittas. Meanwhile, opposition parties have planned to march to the Supreme Court on Monday, with Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge seeking an appointment with Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant to raise the issue of alleged “vote chori”. However, the CJI rejected the INDIA bloc leaders’ request for a meeting. However, CJI has reportedly rejected the request.
